title: Quantis - embeddings + rerank discovery
next_steps: Send detailed pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted TCO spreadsheet
Share SOC2 + SAML + KMS security pack
Run 1-week pilot (10k queries/day) using Quantis dataset - Redwood to provide benchmark guide
Schedule technical deep-dive next week for hybrid search architecture
action_items: Samir Patel - draft benchmark plan and sample scripts (2026-08-20)
Priya Narang - provide sample dataset and QPS targets (2026-08-18)
summary: Initial discovery for embeddings + reranking use case. Quantis wants to evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a hybrid search (semantic + keyword) recommender. Main concerns: throughput (QPS), embedding dimensionality/cost, vector DB integration, encryption/KMS, and audit logs. Agreed to run a 1-week pilot and schedule a technical deep-dive.
topics: security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, data residency
questions: Can Redwood host embeddings and rerank with integrated vector DB?
What's the recommended embedding dimension and model for QA/recs?
How do we measure QPS and latency on Dedicated vs Hosted?
What's included in audit logs and retention?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-17 16:00 PST | Duration 42m | Attendees: Alex Moore (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Quantis, CTO); Priya Narang (Quantis, ML Eng); Marcus Chen (Quantis, Product); Evelyn Ruiz (Quantis, Security)

00:00 Alex: okay everyone thanks for joining, um we appreciate the time. quick intros from our side: alex moore ae, samir patel se, lina torres csm here if you need onboarding stuff later.
00:12 Jordan: hey alex, thanks. Jordan here, CTO at quantis, priya is on she runs our embedding pipelines, marcus product, evelyn security.
00:20 Alex: great, goal today is to understand your use case for embeddings and reranking and figure out hosted vs dedicated vs private fit. high level prior to jump in any constraints?
00:34 Priya: yeah so we have two main flows - question answering from docs and a recommendations / rerank pipeline for product search. currently we use a hybrid search layer: bm25 for recall then cosine on embedding vectors for rerank.
00:47 Marcus: volume is growing fast, we're seeing spikes during promotions, target is ~6k QPS at peak across search endpoints, most queries are small short queries under 64 tokens.
01:00 Samir: 6k peak is helpful, are those concurrent QPS or qps per second? can you break down by endpoint?
01:06 Marcus: rough numbers: search rerank ~3.5k qps peak, qa chat ~1.5k, embeddings upsert about 500 qps during bulk loads.
01:18 Priya: note that our index size is about 80M vectors, 1536-dim embeddings currently from our current model (opensrc).
01:28 Evelyn: from security side we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for key management and logs retained for a year. data residency must stay in us-east for now.
01:41 Alex: all sounds reasonable. quick clarifying question: are you running your own vector DB (pinecone/milvus/elastic) or looking for an integrated solution?
01:50 Jordan: currently running Milvus on k8s, but we've looked at pinecone as managed alternative. open to Redwood handling vector store or integrating with milvus - depends on cost and latency.
02:02 Samir: capability wise, Redwood Hosted provides managed vectors with an optimized runtime for rerank; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for inference and you can keep vectors in your VPC with Private offering full on-prem controls. For 6k qps, Dedicated or Private is likely better for predictable throughput.
02:19 Priya: curious on embedding dimensionality - we use 1536 dims, cost is high. do you recommend smaller dims?
02:26 Samir: common guidance: for general semantic search 768-1536 works; you can often quantize to int8/4 and get good results. sacrifice accuracy vs cost tradeoff - we can run evals on your test set. our optimize toolkit suggests dimensionality reduction or use of a lower-dim model and then measure rerank mrr.
02:44 Marcus: hybrid search question - we want BM25 + embeddings. does Redwood support hybrid? we need to do a combination of lexical scoring then embed-based rerank with score fusion.
02:53 Alex: yes, Redwood supports hybrid search patterns; you can route initial candidate retrieval to your vector DB or elastic then call Redwood rerank model for re-scoring. we also support returning token-level cost breakdowns and latency per route.
03:08 Priya: integration specifics - we currently have milvus self-hosted. what's the typical connector flow? do you push vectors to Redwood or do you keep them in milvus and call Redwood for rerank only?
03:19 Samir: both patterns supported. 1) Push embeddings to Redwood-managed vector store - simpler and lower latency for hosted flows; 2) Keep vectors in your milvus and call Redwood for inference only - we provide a batched rerank API that accepts vectors or ids + fetch.
03:33 Jordan: in pattern 2, fetching id-based vectors adds network hops - would that affect latency? our SLA target for tail p95 is 120ms for rerank.
03:44 Samir: yes fetching adds latency but we use continuous batching and KV cache to reduce round trips. for 120ms p95 at 3.5k qps, you'd likely need Dedicated with colocated vector store or a fast VPC peering private deployment.
03:58 Evelyn: encryption at rest/in transit - if we use Redwood Hosted, who manages KMS keys? can we bring our own?
04:06 Alex: Hosted supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations for enterprise customers, plus SAML SSO for access controls. Private gives you full control of your KMS and audit log storage.
04:18 Marcus: ok pricing - embeddings storage cost vs compute costs for rerank? we need a ballpark to compare milvus on k8s vs Redwood dedicated monthly.
04:26 Alex: we'll send detailed TCO spreadsheet but ballpark: embeddings storage + index maintenance tends to be cheaper self-hosted at modest scale, but when factoring dedicated GPUs, autoscaling, and SLO risk, Dedicated becomes competitive past a few 10s of millions of vectors or high QPS patterns. also caching and quantization reduce token and compute costs significantly.
04:44 Priya: for the pilot we want to simulate production QPS - you mentioned batching - do you have sample benchmark scripts?
04:51 Samir: yes we'll provide a benchmark guide and scripts. typical flow: upsert a slice of your 80M vectors (or a subset), run steady-state qps at target and measure p50/p95, and change batch sizes and quantization profiles. we'll include examples for 1536 -> 768 conversion.
05:07 Jordan: model choice - we saw Redwood has a catalog of verified open models; any recommended embedding models for commerce recs?
05:15 Samir: for commerce and product semantic similarity, 768-dim open models like 's-bison-small' (example name, not exact) or mid-sized 1024/1536 depending on precision. we'll run your evals and produce an MRR chart across dims.
05:30 Priya: reranking approach - do you suggest using the same embedding model for retrieval and rerank or a separate cross-encoder?
05:38 Samir: many teams use a bi-encoder for retrieval and a cross-encoder (rerank) for final re-score. Redwood supports both patterns; cross-encoder is heavier but at lower candidate counts (top-50) it's viable. Dedicated GPUs with batching make cross-encoder cost-effective.
05:55 Marcus: can we do on-demand cross-encoder only for high-value queries?
06:00 Alex: yes, can implement conditional routing based on query type, user segment, or latency budget. Redwood routing policies allow fallbacks to faster model variants.
06:10 Evelyn: audit logs and retention specifics? we need one-year retention and exportable logs for audits.
06:17 Alex: audit logs are available with customizable retention and export. Private deployments can keep logs in your SIEM. Hosted & Dedicated enterprise tiers include longer retention as an add-on.
06:28 Jordan: regulatory/data residency - must be in us-east for now. can Redwood pin region for dedicated?
06:34 Samir: yes you can pin capacity to region. Private gives full region control. Hosted we run in multiple regions but Enterprise can request region-specific placement.
06:44 Priya: any limitations on vector dimensionality - e.g., >2048 dims? we have some experiments at 2048 dims for rich product features.
06:52 Samir: runtime supports up to large dims but memory and index cost scale. with 80M vectors at 2048 dims you'd see big storage jumps; quantization and product quantization (PQ) help. we recommend running a sample conversion to int8/4 and measure recall.
07:10 Marcus: what's the retry/backoff / graceful degradation story during spikes?
07:16 Alex: Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallback models. during capacity stress we can route to cheaper lower-accuracy variants or to cached results; Dedicated offers burst capacity too.
07:28 Priya: for our team, main success criteria: p95 rerank <120ms, MRR > baseline by 8-10% on rerank, cost per 1k queries below $X (tbd).
07:40 Alex: good to capture. we'll work with you on specific numbers in the TCO.
07:46 Jordan: security wants to review the SOC2 docs and network diagram before pilot.
07:51 Evelyn: yes and interface for SSO provisioning, RBAC roles.
07:56 Alex: we'll send security pack including SOC2, data flow diagram, SAML, KMS docs and an architecture note for Private/Dedicated setups.
08:06 Marcus: next steps?
08:09 Alex: recap: 1) Alex will send pricing/TCO and security pack; 2) Samir will provide benchmark plan and scripts; 3) quantis to provide sample dataset and QPS targets; 4) schedule tech deep-dive next week (samir + priya deep dive). agreed?
08:23 Jordan: yep sounds good. thanks.
08:26 Priya: one last nit - latency numbers sometimes vary between our env and cloud. when you do pilot, can you run colocated test?
08:33 Samir: yes we'll do VPC peering test for more realistic latency.
08:37 Alex: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors: model names sometimes garbled (references to 's-bison-small' are approximate), product names like milvus/pinecone sometimes mis-transcribed, speaker crosstalk near decisions.

End of call.
